text:
elaine: Quick check — post-launch grooming plan for the Search Suggest rollout. Need a clear rule: which bugs get hotfixed vs pushed to backlog, and what our follow-on milestone cadence is. 2-week hotfix window? Thoughts?

sam: +1 to a short hotfix window. Only P0 regressions should be hotfixed. Anything else goes into the next sprint unless customer escalation.

devon: Proposed triage rubric:
```
P0 - blocks core user flows (login/search results missing): HOTFIX within 48h
P1 - major degradation (significant perf regressions, frequent errors): next patch/expedite
P2 - minor bugs/usability: backlog, next normal sprint
P3 - cosmetic/edge: low priority
``` 

mike: Also: we need concrete telemetry thresholds to auto-trigger paging/rollback. My suggestion: error rate >5% sustained for 10m OR success-rate drop >8% vs baseline -> rollback/canary pause.

aya: For customer-driven asks — two enterprise customers asked for variant weighting and richer snippet fields. Those are follow-on milestones, not hotfixes. Recommend we include them in M2 (next 4-week milestone) and offer interim workarounds.

sam: Operational constraint: freeze schema/canonical index changes for any hotfix branch. Keep changes small and easily revertible.

devon: Owners and rough timeline:
- Hotfix owner: @mike (cut branch today, tests tomorrow)
- Customer features: @aya (scoping this week, M2 planning)
- QA/Release: @sam (canary to 10% then ramp)

mike: I'll cut the hotfix branch now: `git checkout -b hotfix/search-suggest-1.0.1` && `./scripts/run-smoke.sh` — will post results here.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: hotfix/search-suggest-1.0.1 -> canary (10%) by @sam

elaine: Great. Can we have a one-pager with acceptance criteria for hotfix vs M2 features by EOD? I'll consolidate and send to ENG/CS.

aya: I'll draft the one-pager and include CS asks + sample rollback plan.

sam: Thanks — if no objections, we ship hotfix after canary checks. :thumbsup:
